recipe.notes:
The paper's second judge. Client block: max_output_tokens 8192, context_tokens 131072 (the checkpoint's own maximum via YARN factor 32, and the engine's --max-model-len), concurrency 256, decoding json_schema. Text-only: no image_processor, no max_images. Sampling (2026-10-10 owner decision, superseding decision 4.3's paper sampling): the checkpoint's own generation_config.json at the pinned revision declares no sampling parameters -- only bos_token_id, eos_token_id, pad_token_id, do_sample and transformers_version -- so the recipe sends temperature 0.0 (greedy; the config-without-sampling-parameters rule) and no top_p/top_k. The paper's gpt-oss clients also declared `temperature: 0.0` (configs/model/gpt_oss_120b/client.yaml and client.pool.yaml), so the temperature matches the paper's runs; the paper's second-judge runs drove the pooled client with the tournament's `max_response_tokens: 12288` where this recipe keeps the preset's 8192 (a DECLARED DIVERGENCE, recorded). temperature and max_output_tokens are CONTENT fields of the judgement family, so this sampling change re-keys the family (the owner accepted the re-key): a judgement recorded before it never pools with one recorded after -- see handover/reports/08bd-judge-recipes.md. Serving: vLLM's name for this checkpoint's reasoning parser is `openai_gptoss` (SGLang's was `gpt-oss`); vLLM also auto-selects it when unset, and the recipe declares it explicitly. No media flags. Memory arithmetic, both GPU classes (GiB, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 default; the paper set none here). Weights 65.2 GB on disk (65 248 815 744 B over the index's 15 shards: 57.3 GB packed MXFP4 + 3.6 GB E8M0 scales + 4.3 GB BF16, for 116 829 156 672 parameters; the repo's original/ BF16 copies are not loaded). - B200 (192 GB; 0.92 -> 176.6 GB budget): TP1 -> 65.2 GB weights, ~111 GB cache. KV (BF16): 18 full-attention
  layers x 2 x 8 KV heads x 64 head_dim x 2 B = 36 864 B/token; at TP1 all 8 heads sit on the one GPU, so a
  full-length 131 072-token sequence ~4.5 GiB -- ~24 full-length sequences (or ~350 typical 2k-token windows).
  The 18 sliding-window layers hold at most their 128-token window each (~4.7 MB/sequence, negligible). No
  linear-attention state. resources.gpus: 1; throughput scales by replicas.
- H100 (80 GB; 0.92 -> 73.6 GB budget): TP1 fits too (65.2 GB weights, ~8.4 GB cache), so the shape is the
  same -- no `--set` override is needed; the cache is tight (~1.8 full-length sequences, thousands of 2k
  windows), and a denser node runs one replica per GPU. Hopper serves MXFP4 natively.
History: the paper served this judge as TP4 x DP2 on 8x B200 in its pooled configuration (the second-judge TREC-DL run); the decision-41 shape is one TP1 replica per engine, scaled by replicas. Engine support: GptOssForCausalLM is in vLLM v0.31.0's registry (registry.py:123, module gpt_oss); the pin equals the Hub head (checked 2026-10-09). status: unverified until the E2 judge wave passes (decision 1).

The paper's pin, equal to the Hub head at the check date. The served name is the recipe id; the T4 scenarios override it to their slot name at run time. B200 and H100: TP1 (resources.gpus 1).
